clue.text: Desire for public transport in Tennessee?

definitions.text: Desire for public transport in Tennessee?

parts.words: Desire for public transport in Tennessee?
parts.note: Tennessee Williams wrote a play named after a New Orleans tram called Desire, so the clue reads 'Desire' as the name of a vehicle in his work

explanation.surface: Someone in Tennessee longing for a bus or train service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tennessee' looks like the US state but is the playwright Tennessee Williams, whose play A Streetcar Named Desire names a tram line in New Orleans.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Williams play, Desire is the name on the tram line, a vehicle of public transport.

clue.text: Woodland god to some extent displays a tyrannical streak

indicators.note: to some extent means only part of the words displays a tyrannical gives the letters

explanation.surface: A forest deity shows some cruel tendencies.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a half-man, half-goat creature of the woods attending Dionysus.

clue.text: Dress again in regal turnout

indicators.note: turnout suggests the letters of in regal are turned out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Getting changed into royal attire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnout' rearranges IN REGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress troops is to line them up, so dressing again is lining up anew.

clue.text: Almost condescend, being spoilt, to be settled comfortably

indicators.note: being spoilt means the remaining letters are messed up and rearranged
almost means the word condescend stops short of its last letter

explanation.surface: Nearly patronising, being pampered, to be cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts CONDESCEND to CONDESCEN; 'being spoilt' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tucked snugly in a safe or comfortable place is to be settled comfortably.

clue.text: Observation about character in part of the railway carriage

indicators.note: about means around, so the observation goes round the character

parts.note: a comment is an observation or remark
a part is a role or character in a play

explanation.surface: A remark about someone's role inside a train.
explanation.definitionFit: A separate enclosed section of a carriage, with its own seats and door.

clue.text: Fabulous bird takes up French horn

indicators.note: takes up means the letters are lifted backwards in this down light

parts.note: cor is French for horn

explanation.surface: A legendary bird learns to play a brass instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French horn' looks like the instrument but is the French word for horn, COR.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant mythical bird from Arabian tales, fabulous in the sense of legendary.

clue.text: Odds on cash being provided for a burlesque

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
oof is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A bookmaker's odds set on money paid to fund a comic stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque is a mocking imitation, the same as a parody or send-up.

clue.text: Found a bituminous substance in the street

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
tar is a black bituminous material

explanation.surface: Discovering tar on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' reads as discovered, but it is the sense of establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To found something is to establish or begin it.

clue.text: Point of view a student in Oxford University accepted

indicators.note: in places the student letter inside the run

parts.note: took means accepted
L is a learner, a student, from L-plates

explanation.surface: An undergraduate's opinion is received at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner, from the L-plates British learner drivers display.
explanation.definitionFit: A perspective or attitude is a way of looking at things.

clue.text: Set of transparencies, initially from one old railway journey

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word from

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
LMS is the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, an old British company
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: Slides taken on a trip on a historic railway.
explanation.walkthrough: The LMS was one of Britain's big railway companies before nationalisation in 1948.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of film with still pictures projected one by one, like a set of slides.

clue.text: He's left the redemption money in the bar

indicators.note: left here means gone away, so the letters of He depart from the word next to them

parts.note: the clue word He supplies the two letters that go
money paid to free a hostage is a ransom

explanation.surface: A kidnapper leaves the ransom in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's left the' means HE has left THE, leaving T; 'in the bar' looks like a place, but 'bar' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosspiece of wood or stone over a door or window is a horizontal beam, a kind of bar.

clue.text: Where hops are dried in the Golden State by the sea

indicators.note: in here asks for one piece to be placed inside another

parts.note: California is the Golden State, abbreviated CAL
an oast is a kiln for drying hops, familiar in Kent

explanation.surface: Asking where in California the hops are dried, near the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: An OAST is the kiln used in England for drying hops for beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seaside lies along the shore, beside the ocean.

clue.text: Small animal an Athenian character kept at home

indicators.note: kept means held, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character an Athenian would write
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A Greek keeps a little pet in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' is the setter's joke: the beast is huge, though its two-letter-shortened slang form also names money.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros, a thick-skinned horned beast, is usually shortened to this name.

clue.text: Powerful sea bird is well below par

definitions.meaning: a large, strong-winged seabird of the southern oceans
in golf, a score three strokes under par on a hole

explanation.surface: A strong seabird is in poor health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'below par' suggests feeling unwell, but in golf it means a good score: this one is three under par on a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The great wandering seabird gives its name to golf's rare three-under-par score, better than an eagle.

clue.text: Surpass a comedy actor's popular books

parts.note: to best someone is to surpass them
Peter Sellers was a British comic actor

explanation.surface: Outdoing a comedian's well-liked books.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Sellers was a British comedy actor, famous as Inspector Clouseau.
explanation.definitionFit: Books that sell in huge numbers are the popular ones.

clue.text: Vessel taking peacekeepers across river

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the peacekeepers stretch over the river letter

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

explanation.surface: A ship carries UN troops over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel is a container, and this one is a vase or a large tea pot.

clue.text: Not fit for hunt, he lay injured

indicators.note: injured means the letters of hunt he lay are damaged into a new order

explanation.surface: A rider unable to ride to hounds, having lain hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' rearranges HUNT HE LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in poor health is not fit.

clue.text: E.g. Westminster clerk is unusually tricky fellow

parts.note: Westminster is an example of a city

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of clerk is are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A London civil servant is surprisingly crafty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges CLERK IS into SLICKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth, sophisticated urban type, often thought sharp or untrustworthy, is a tricky fellow.

clue.text: Not even guerillas are troops of this sort

definitions.text: guerillas are troops of this sort
definitions.meaning: guerilla fighters are soldiers outside the regular army

explanation.surface: Guerilla fighters are not part of a uniform army.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both uneven and describes soldiers not in a standing army.

clue.text: Musical theatre employee possibly creating a bang

definitions.meaning: a dresser working on the rock musical Hair
a bang is a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead

explanation.surface: A stagehand might cause an explosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bang' suggests an explosion, but it is the American word for a fringe of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre dresser helps actors into costume, so one at the show Hair fits; a salon stylist cuts fringes.

clue.text: Ask for popular papers

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: Requesting the tabloid newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popular papers' suggests tabloid newspapers; a quire is a printer's measure of about two dozen sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask is to seek information, to query.

clue.text: Work follows — fine and dandy

indicators.note: follows means the work comes after the fine letter

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Things go well once the job comes in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine and dandy' reads as a happy phrase; 'dandy' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dandy is a man excessively concerned with clothes and looks.

clue.text: Highwayman in need of a corn-plaster?

definitions.text: Highwayman in need of a corn-plaster?

parts.words: Highwayman in need of a corn-plaster?
parts.note: an old word for a robber on foot is read as a cushion for a sore toe

explanation.surface: A robber with sore feet.
explanation.walkthrough: An old word for a robber on foot, read literally as a pad for the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who robbed travellers on foot rather than horseback was a highway robber.

clue.text: Account or short story about desert deliverance

indicators.note: about means around, so the account and shortened story go round the desert word
short means the word for story loses its last letter

parts.note: a tale is a story
to desert is to quit

explanation.surface: A tale of being rescued in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Account or short story' reads as a choice between two things; 'or' is only a link, and 'short' and 'about' are both indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal verdict of not guilty releases the accused, a formal deliverance from the charge.

clue.text: Island youth — one included in an epic poem

indicators.note: included in means one letter is placed inside the youth

parts.note: a lad is a youth
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A young islander features in an ancient epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic about the siege of Troy.

clue.text: Write for another? That's the spirit

definitions.meaning: to produce a book that is published under someone else's name
a spectre or apparition of the dead

explanation.surface: Asking whether writing for someone else is the right attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's the spirit' reads as encouragement; 'spirit' is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden writer is called by the same word as a phantom, both unseen presences.

clue.text: Negotiate terms for a school outing, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a special outing given as a pleasure

explanation.surface: Bargaining over a class trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to bargain with someone and a special pleasure such as a day out.

clue.text: Insight abandoned in teaching

indicators.note: abandoned means the word in is given up from the synonym for insight

parts.note: intuition is insight, instinctive understanding

explanation.surface: Understanding is given up in the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is the piece abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Instruction given by a tutor, as in school fees, is teaching.

clue.text: River rising in this sleepy land

indicators.note: rising means the river's letters go upwards in this down light

parts.note: the Don is a river in Yorkshire and in Russia

explanation.surface: A river has its source in the land of sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: The Land of Nod is the proverbial land of sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The Land of Nod, from Genesis, is used for the state of sleep.

clue.text: City margins we finally surpass

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district
lips are the edges or margins of a cup or crater

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of we

explanation.surface: Our city's outer areas will end up beating others.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postcode area of the City of London, its financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine something is to surpass it, as the moon blots out the sun.

clue.text: Return and surrender

definitions.meaning: a profit or return on investment

explanation.surface: Coming back and giving in.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a financial gain from investment and giving way to an opponent.

clue.text: Record studied for sound — it's a disgrace!

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: for sound means the word for studied is taken by how it is pronounced

parts.note: read means studied, as at university
the clue word it supplies its own letters

explanation.surface: Someone looked over a recording to check its audio quality and found it shameful.
explanation.walkthrough: READ in its past tense is pronounced 'red'; 'for sound' gives that spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of reputation brings shame, so it is a dishonour or disgrace.
